newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo orange crop still seen at 352 mln boxes.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo orange crop still seen at 352 mln boxes.

text.p: Brazil's Association of Citrus Exporters (Abecitrus) is to leave unchanged its May estimate of the 1996/97 Sao Paulo orange crop of 352 million 40.8 kg boxes, said the association's president.
"We are going to keep the same figure, that is 352 million boxes with 105 million for the domestic market and 247 million to be processed for juice," said Ademerval Garcia.
The association would next issue a crop forecast in December, he added.
According to Abecitrus, the 1996/97 crop is only slightly down on the 1995/96 harvest of 357 million boxes.

Weekly figures from Abecitrus show production to be running well up from last season, totalling 437,840 tonnes to September 22 against 252,888 tonnes to September 24, 1995 but this is because the 1995/96 season began late, Garcia said.
Exports are also running on a par to last year, he said.
In the 1995/96 crop year (July/June), Brazil exported a total of 1.032 million tonnes of frozen concentrated orange juice, virtually unchanged from 1.038 million in 1994/95.
But market share changed slightly, with European sales up to 711,200 tonnes against 643,600 tonnes the previous year, making up for a drop in sales to the U.S., Japan and Korea.
Exports to the U.S. finished at 188,300 tonnes, down from the 213,600 tonnes exported in 1994/95 but well above initial gloomy expectations of only 65,000 tonnes.
The increase has been attributed to cold weather which hit the U.S. crop and a color problem which has necessitated purchases of Brazilian juice for blending.

In contrast, Japanese sales had been hoped to reach 85,000 tonnes but instead, hit by the economic situation and an unfavorable dollar/yen exchange rate, totalled 66,500 tonnes, well down from the 95,600 tonnes purchased in 1994/95.
Korea, the other main buyer, also saw sales fall to 26,400 tonnes in 1995/96 from 47,500 tonnes the previous year.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
